Subject: Visibility & runbook: per-slice sampling + cost reconciliation for high-cost spikes

Team —

Following last week's outage postmortem for ACME (spike in inference cost + tail latency), product asked me to draft a scoped request so we can prioritize Console work in Q2. Goal: give customers (and our SREs) a way to see why a tenant/route suddenly balloons in cost and to have an operator playbook to stabilize traffic.

Proposed high-level asks:
- Expose per-slice sampling controls in Console (sample rate, sampling windows) so customers can reduce token-level telemetry for noisy routes.
- Add a per-route cost breakdown: tokens, GPU-seconds (or equivalent), cache-hit savings, and billing vs console delta for last 24/72 hours.
- Provide an automated exception playbook when cost exceeds threshold: steps, temporary mitigations (sample-rate override, fallback model), owner, and required telemetry to collect.

Attached is a quick proposal (sample-rate-proposal.pdf) and a reconciliation workbook (cost-reconciliation-spreadsheet.xlsx) with example rows from ACME last week. Bethany — can you confirm which billing keys we should reconcile against (invoice line items vs internal usage tags)?

Asks for this thread:
1) Engineering: feasibility + rough ETA (Markus)
2) Product/Console: exact UX scope + permissions model (Lauren)
3) SRE/Security: any blockers for adding sampling toggles + runbook automation (Grace)

I think we can scope an MLP that surfaces a 'cost spike' card on the tenant view with the items above + a one-click 'apply temporary sample-rate' action.

Thanks — Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Visibility & runbook: per-slice sampling + cost reconciliation for high-cost spikes

Tessa — thanks for the clear brief and the attachments. Quick thoughts from runtime/serving side:

- Sampling toggles: technically straightforward if we expose policy flags per-tenant + route; the tricky bit is applying overrides without invalidating KV cache heuristics. We can implement a transient sampling layer on top of batching that adjusts telemetry emission (not model inputs) first.
- Cost breakdown: we already capture per-request token counts and per-batch GPU time; building a dashboard that aggregates these by route and maps to billable units should be doable. The reconciliation delta often comes from reserved capacity amortization and network egress lines — we should document those discrepancies.

Questions:
1) When you say 'one-click apply temporary sample-rate' — is that a Console-only action scoped to the tenant (i.e., admin role) or should we allow customer admins to invoke it?
2) What SLAs for 'rollback' do we expect after an override is applied?

I can spin up a spike branch and a minimal API by EOW to demonstrate prototype metrics. I'll file a Jira and include the proposed telemetry schema.

Markus

Thanks Tessa — ACME would appreciate per-tenant controls. A few notes:

- For reconciliation: please reconcile against our invoice item 'inference.compute' and the 'tenant_id' tag we send via metadata. We had an internal spreadsheet showing a ~12% delta last week; I'll attach that in a follow-up if helpful.
- Permissioning: customer admins should be able to propose a sample-rate change but it should be gated (either require a 2nd sign-off from our side or only allow a temporary window unless we approve permanent changes).
- Runbook: we need clear escalation paths. When we hit a spike we want to know whether it's model-level (prompts, prompt storms), traffic-level (bad-client loop), or system-level (cache miss regressions). If the console can auto-classify the likely root cause it would speed up mitigation.

Happy to jump on a 30m sync to walk through our invoice lines and share our internal numbers — we can do Tuesday morning PST.

—Bethany
Senior Product Ops, Acme Analytics

I sketched a minimal UX flow for the MLP:

- Tenant view: 'Cost Spike' card with top N contributing routes, estimated incremental cost per route, and an indicator for cache-hit ratio.
- Action menu for each route: Preview sample-rate impact (estimate tokens saved), Apply temporary override (select duration), Send to ops (creates incident and pings on-call).
- Permissions: Only 'tenant_admin_proposed' can propose; 'tenant_admin_confirm' or Redwood CS can approve. That matches Bethany's ask.

I'll attach the mock screenshots to the Drive doc and link the sketch in the Jira ticket. UX questions: do we want the 'Preview sample-rate impact' to run a historical simulation (sample against last 24h) or present a conservative estimate? Historical sim is more useful but heavier to compute.

Lauren

Summary and next steps (agreeing to scope and owners):

1) Jira: OBS-9421 created by Markus (spike + prototype).
2) Prototype goals (Markus): API to toggle sampling, telemetry schema, and a lightweight historical simulator for 'preview' (POC by 2028-02-24).
3) Console UX (Lauren): implement Cost Spike card + route action menu. Sketches + mock links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcD-example-doc (in related_links).
4) Runbook (Tessa/Grace): draft a one-page playbook with triage questions (model vs traffic vs system), immediate mitigations (apply sample-rate, route fallback to smaller model, enable prefix caching), and escalation contacts. Draft due 2028-02-22.
5) Billing reconciliation (Tessa + Bethany): Bethany to share invoice mapping; Tessa to add reconciliation columns to cost-reconciliation-spreadsheet.xlsx.

I also attached the sample-rate-proposal.pdf with the operational constraints we should enforce (max override duration, audit logs required). Note: Security flagged that any console action which affects runtime behavior must be logged to the audit pipeline — not optional.

If there are no objections I'll move this to the OBS sprint board and set the initial story points.

Grace

Redwood Inference
